Weekend workout: French writing and listening challenges for Friday 6th November 2026 - Student Life

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:40
Instaread

Thanks for being a Premium KwizIQ French subscriber. It's time for your Weekend Workout with a mix of writing challenges, dictations and our new comprehension exercises.

This week's theme is Student Life. 

 

Writing Challenges:

  • B1: Studying programme
  • C1: If you could learn anything instantly...

Dictées:

  • A1: Nos sujets préférés à l'université
  • A2: Choisir ses études
  • B2: Un lycée en piteux état

 

NEW! Comprehension exercises:

  • B1: Partir étudier à l'étranger - les qualités à avoir
  • B2: La rentrée, quelle angoisse !

 

What's new: comprehension exercises

Every Interactive Reader now ends with a comprehension exercise, so you can check how much of the text you really took in. Read the text (with or without grammar hints), then click "Start comprehension exercise" and answer a few questions about what happened, who did what and why.

 

You answer in English, on purpose: this exercise checks your understanding only, not your spelling or grammar. For each answer you'll see whether you got it, partly got it or missed it, along with what the text actually said. The questions match the CEFR level of the Reader, so pick your level or go up a notch for a challenge.

As a Premium member, you have full access to comprehension exercises across the whole library of Interactive Readers.

 

How do challenges and dictations work?

Writing challenges and dictations are self-scoring exercises, meaning that for each phrase you'll be offered corrections to help you pinpoint your mistakes, but the marking is up to you!

 

Once you're done, you can read and listen to the full text in French, and also see a list of grammar topics covered in the exercise.

Comprehension exercises work a little differently: you answer in English and get instant feedback on each answer, so you know exactly which parts of the text you understood.

Remember if you want to kwiz any of the lessons again, you can add them to your notebook(s).
